label: Formulated the metaphysics of Light and knowledge by presence (al-'ilm al-huduri)
description: Suhrawardi founded the Illuminationist school (Hikmat al-Ishraq), demonstrating that knowledge by presence (unmediated, reflexive self-awareness) is the foundational condition of all knowledge, replacing Peripatetic substance with the ontology of Light.
historicalContext: Articulated in 12th-century Aleppo and Persia as a radical reform of post-Avicennian scholasticism.
dialecticalTension: Overturns Peripatetic representational epistemology (knowledge by acquired form) in favor of immediate, luminous self-manifestation.

citations.author: Shahab al-Din Suhrawardi
citations.quote: Light is that which is evident in itself and brings other things to evidence. Nothing is more evident than Light.

citations.author: Mehdi Ha'iri Yazdi
citations.work: The Principles of Epistemology in Islamic Philosophy: Knowledge by Presence

label: Critiqued Avicenna's essentialist definitions and Peripatetic noetics
description: Suhrawardi took Avicenna's 'Floating Man' argument to its radical conclusion, showing that immediate self-awareness disproves the Aristotelian claim that self-knowledge requires a formal definition through genus and specific difference.
historicalContext: Suhrawardi's dialectical engagement with Avicenna's Kitab al-Shifa and Oriental Philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Demonstrates that discursive definition leads to infinite regress unless grounded in direct intuitive presence.

citations.author: Shahab al-Din Suhrawardi
citations.quote: If you do not know yourself through direct presence, no definition composed of genus and difference can ever make you know yourself.

citations.author: Hossein Ziai
citations.work: Knowledge and Illumination: A Study of Suhrawardi's Hikmat al-Ishraq

label: Revived the Platonic Forms as Archetypal Lights (Muthul Nuriya)
description: Suhrawardi claimed to revive the perennial wisdom (al-hikmah al-laduniyyah) of ancient sages, reinterpreting Platonic Forms as living, conscious Archetypal Lights residing in the imaginal realm ('alam al-mithal).
historicalContext: The deliberate integration of pre-Socratic, Platonic, and ancient Persian Hermetic wisdom in 12th-century Islamic philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Replaces static, abstract Platonic Forms with dynamic, self-conscious luminous hypostases.

citations.author: John Walbridge
citations.work: The Leaven of the Ancients: Suhrawardi and the Heritage of the Greeks

label: Supplied the ontology of the imaginal realm ('alam al-mithal)
description: Suhrawardi's formulation of the autonomous, intermediate imaginal world ('alam al-mithal)—where spiritual entities take material shape and physical entities become subtle—deeply influenced Ibn Arabi's mystical cosmology.
historicalContext: The eastern transmission of Illuminationist concepts to the Andalusian and Syrian Sufi traditions in the early 13th century.
dialecticalTension: Ibn Arabi grounds Suhrawardi's world of images in the comprehensive ontology of the divine names and the Unity of Being.

citations.author: Henry Corbin
citations.work: Alone with the Alone: Creative Imagination in the Sufism of Ibn 'Arabi

label: Provided the Illuminationist pillars of Transcendent Theosophy
description: Mulla Sadra wrote an extensive commentary on Suhrawardi's Hikmat al-Ishraq, adopting Suhrawardi's concepts of knowledge by presence and ontological gradation while shifting the primary substrate from essence to existence.
historicalContext: The philosophical synthesis of the Safavid School of Isfahan in 17th-century Persia.
dialecticalTension: Mulla Sadra critiques Suhrawardi's essentialism (asalat al-mahiyyah), transposing Suhrawardi's gradation of Light into the gradation of Being (tashkik al-wujud).

citations.author: Sajjad H. Rizvi
citations.work: Mulla Sadra and Metaphysics: Modulation of Being
